title: Personal mini lab worksheet — latency heuristics
content:
Mini worksheet for quick runs — keep terse, single-page capture for morning tinkering.

Purpose:
- Quick compare of small config tweaks (batch size, kv cache hit policy, quant) to understand p50/p95 shifts for 1–2k token tails.
- Capture one actionable hypothesis per session so I don't over-index on noisy variance.

Notes to self:
- Use same seed prompts set (~/prompts/heuristic-sample-24.txt).
- Warmup with 3 short requests before measuring.
- Record cost calc using local token-meter (approx pricing: $0.0006 / 1k tokens hosted baseline).
- Run IDs use format RYYMMDD-XX.

Quick results table (top of sheet):
| run_id | date | model | seq_len | batch | quant | kv_cache | p50_ms | p95_ms | tokens_out | est_cost_per_1k | notes | next_action |
| R250602-01 | 2025-06-02 | redwood-open-7b | 1024 | 1 | fp16 | off | 78 | 210 | 420 | $0.0006 | baseline, stable | try batch=4 |
| R250602-02 | 2025-06-02 | redwood-open-7b | 1024 | 4 | fp16 | off | 92 | 245 | 420 | $0.0005 | higher p95 from batching overhead | test kv_cache=prefix|
| R250609-01 | 2025-06-09 | redwood-open-7b-q4_0 | 1024 | 1 | q4_0 | off | 60 | 180 | 410 | $0.00037 | quant helped p50, small token loss on completions | validate quality on eval set|
| R250614-03 | 2025-06-14 | redwood-open-7b-q4_0 | 1024 | 1 | q4_0 | prefix | 45 | 130 | 410 | $0.00037 | kv cache reduced p50 significantly for repeating prefixes | increase batch to 2 and re-run|

Observations (raw):
- kv cache (prefix policy) gives largest p50 wins on repeating-prompt workloads — good for chat assistants with repeated system/user prefixes.
- batching helps throughput but can push p95 if not paired with smaller batch windows or adaptive micro-batching.
- q4_0 quant reduces p50 and cost materially; need small quality check (BLEU-like on fill tasks) — quick inspection shows mostly fine for short completions.

Actionable hypotheses (top 3):
1) For low-latency assistants, default to q4_0 + kv-prefix + batch=1; use local short-term cache TTL 30s for very hot prefixes. (Plan: R250616-01 run series)
2) For high-throughput batched workloads, enable batch=4 with adaptive release when queue latency > 80ms to guard p95. (Plan: simulate load and instrument p95 triggers)
3) For safety, include lightweight eval after rollout: 200 prompts sampled from prod traces, ensure reply-change rate < 1.5% vs fp16 baseline.

Checklist before any larger experiment: 
- [ ] Push prompt set revision to branch and link PR
- [ ] Confirm no-longer-needed snapshots cleared (cost)
- [ ] Tag run artifacts with run_id in S3 and add brief note to ENG-1428

Appendix — quick measurement method: 
- Endpoint: localhost:8080/v1/generate (dev harness)
- Measurement: median of 25 measured requests after 3 warmups; p95 computed from same sample.
- Cost calc: (tokens_in+tokens_out)/1000 * price_per_1k; record est_cost_per_1k cell above.

Open questions / TODOs:
- How to automatically surface kv-cache hit ratios per request in the console? (file a small feature request)
- Should we include a synthetic long-tail prompt to stress p95? Add R250620-LL test.

End of worksheet — quick log of last edits:

2025-06-09 added quant runs.
2025-06-14 added kv-cache prefix runs and update next actions.
